SELECT
    c."name" AS company_name,
    b."name" AS building_name,
    ol."move_in_year",
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.id ORDER BY b."Height" DESC) AS height_rank
FROM "Office_locations" ol
JOIN "Companies" c ON ol.company_id = c.id
JOIN "buildings" b ON ol.building_id = b.id
WHERE b."Status" = 'under construction'
  AND CAST(c."Market_Value_billion" AS REAL) > 300
ORDER BY height_rank ASC;

WITH max_year_cte AS (

)
SELECT c.name AS company_name,
       b.name AS building_name,
       (m.max_year - o.move_in_year) AS years_here
FROM "Office_locations" o
JOIN "Companies" c ON o.company_id = c.id
JOIN "buildings" b ON o.building_id = b.id
CROSS JOIN max_year_cte m
WHERE o.move_in_year >= m.max_year - 2;

    JOIN Companies c ON ol.company_id = c.id
    JOIN buildings b ON ol.building_id = b.id

WITH ordered AS (
        SELECT "Profits_billion",
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "Profits_billion") AS rn,
               COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
        FROM "Companies"
    ),
    median AS (
        SELECT AVG("Profits_billion") AS med
        FROM ordered
        WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2)
    )

JOIN "Office_locations" o ON c."id" = o."company_id"
JOIN "buildings" b ON o."building_id" = b."id"
WHERE c."Profits_billion" > (SELECT med FROM median);

questions.nlq: Could you tell me which companies have a high number of office locations in buildings taller than 200 meters?

meanings.hidden_knowledge: For this question, "high number" means more than three office locations.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT c.name
FROM "Companies" c
JOIN "Office_locations" o ON c.id = o.company_id
JOIN "buildings" b ON o.building_id = b.id
WHERE b."Height" > 200
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: For this question, "high number" means being in the top 25 % of office-location counts among all companies (i.e., at least the 75th‑percentile of the counts).
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH company_counts AS (
    SELECT o.company_id,
           c."name" AS company_name,
           COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM "Office_locations" o
    JOIN "buildings" b ON o.building_id = b.id
    JOIN "Companies" c ON o.company_id = c.id
    WHERE b."Height" > 200
    GROUP BY o.company_id
),
ordered AS (
    SELECT company_name,
           cnt,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY cnt) AS rn,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM company_counts) AS total
    FROM company_counts
),
threshold AS (
    SELECT MIN(cnt) AS thresh
    FROM ordered
    WHERE rn > total * 0.75
)
SELECT company_name
FROM company_counts
WHERE cnt >= (SELECT thresh FROM threshold);

SELECT DISTINCT b.name
FROM buildings b
JOIN Office_locations o ON b.id = o.building_id
JOIN Companies c ON o.company_id = c.id
WHERE c."Profits_billion" > 15;

SELECT DISTINCT b."name" 
FROM "buildings" b
JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b."id" = ol."building_id"
JOIN "Companies" c ON ol."company_id" = c."id"
WHERE c."Profits_billion" > 15;
SELECT DISTINCT b."name" FROM "buildings" b JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b."id" = ol."building_id" JOIN "Companies" c ON ol."company_id" = c."id" WHERE c."Profits_billion" > 15;

WITH top_companies AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM (
        SELECT id, NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY "Profits_billion") AS quintile
        FROM "Companies"
    )
    WHERE quintile = 5
)
SELECT DISTINCT b.name
FROM "buildings" b
JOIN "Office_locations" o ON b.id = o.building_id
JOIN top_companies tc ON o.company_id = tc.id;

WITH RankedCompanies AS (
    SELECT 
        id,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Profits_billion DESC) as row_num,
        COUNT(*) OVER () as total_count
    FROM Companies
),
Top20PercentCompanies AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM RankedCompanies
    WHERE row_num <= total_count * 0.2
)
SELECT DISTINCT b.name
FROM Office_locations ol
JOIN Buildings b ON ol.building_id = b.id
JOIN Top20PercentCompanies tpc ON ol.company_id = tpc.id

WITH profit_ranked AS (
  SELECT "id",
         NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY "Profits_billion" DESC) AS profit_tile
  FROM "Companies"
)
SELECT "b"."name"
FROM "buildings" AS "b"
JOIN "Office_locations" AS "ol" ON "b"."id" = "ol"."building_id"
JOIN "Companies" AS "c" ON "ol"."company_id" = "c"."id"
JOIN profit_ranked AS "pr" ON "c"."id" = "pr"."id"
WHERE "pr"."profit_tile" = 1
GROUP BY "b"."name";

WITH industry_avg AS (
    SELECT "Industry", AVG("Sales_billion") AS avg_sales
    FROM "Companies"
    GROUP BY "Industry"
)

FROM "Companies" C
JOIN industry_avg IA ON C."Industry" = IA."Industry"
JOIN "Office_locations" OL ON C."id" = OL."company_id"
JOIN "Buildings" B ON OL."building_id" = B."id"
WHERE C."Sales_billion" > IA.avg_sales

meanings.gt_sql:
WITH company_quartile AS (
    SELECT
        id,
        name,
        NTILE(4) OVER (PARTITION BY "Industry" ORDER BY "Sales_billion") AS quartile
    FROM "Companies"
)
SELECT
    name
FROM company_quartile
WHERE quartile = 4
  AND id IN (
    SELECT ol."company_id"
    FROM "Office_locations" ol
    JOIN "buildings" b ON ol."building_id" = b."id"
    WHERE b."Status" = 'under construction'
  );
